The *Hāravibhaṅgapañcamabhūmi* ("The Fifth Stage: Analytical Modes of Conveying") forms the fifth chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa*, an exegetical treatise belonging to the late stratum of the Pali Sutta canon. The text sets out an analytical exposition of the hermeneutical conveyances (*hāra*) employed for the interpretation and categorization of the Buddha's teachings.

 The text also shares thematic links and citations with other chapters of the *Netti* (including Ne 8 *Lakkhaṇahāravibhaṅga* and Ne 9 *Catubyūhahāravibhaṅga*), canonical suttas and verses (e.g., SN 1.29, SN 2.28, Ja 520, and Dhp 21, 22, 293), and non-Pali parallels in the Chinese Āgamas (such as SĀ 588 and SĀ2 172), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, the Patna Dharmapada, and Tibetan and Sanskrit recensions of the *Udānavarga*.

According to computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus, the *Hāravibhaṅgapañcamabhūmi* shares 2,742 matching passages across 137 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, its most significant textual correspondences occur with the *Hārasampātabhūmi* (Pe 8), the *Yamaka* (*Uppādavāra*, Ya 10.2.1), the *Vibhaṅga* (*Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga*, Vb 6), the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1), as well as the commentaries and subcommentaries to the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Nettivibhāvinī*) and Majjhima Nikāya [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus show passages shared with Sanskrit texts (including Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā*, the *Patna Dharmapada*, and the Subaši *Udānavarga*), Tibetan canonical and commentarial texts (such as the *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśaṭīkā* and *Madhyamakāvatāraṭīkā*), and the Chinese *Dīrgha Āgama* (*Cháng āhán jīng*, T 1) [DharmaNexus].
